newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Quality seen low in Ukraine wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Quality seen low in Ukraine wheat crop.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE WHEAT CROP STILL SEEN 19-21 MLN TNS, BUT QUALITY LOW
KIEV, Aug 18 - Our forecast for wheat output remains virtually unchanged at around 19-21 million tonnes (compared to 13.55 million tonnes in 1996).
However, estimates of milling wheat output are reduced by 0.8-1.0 million tonnes to 6-7 million tonnes.

As a result, Ukraine in 1997/98 could increase its exports of feed wheat to 1.5 million tonnes. Real export volumes will depend on how competitive Ukrainian prices are in comparison with exports from other countries, chiefly Russia.
The beginning of the harvest in Ukraine coincided with long heavy rains, accompanied in many cases by hail and strong winds.

The wet weather has sharply reduced the quality of the wheat crop. On the whole, the grain being harvested is 5th grade, especially grain in the forest-steppe zone. Moreover, the combination of high humidity and warm weather has brought about a rapid increase in weeds, diseases and pests.
According to the Institute for Plant Defence, a great deal of wheat might be unfit even for use as animal feed as a result of diseases.
At the same time, a high level of soil moisture has increased yields in comparison with the two previous years, in which very dry conditions prevailed.

However, at the end of July, average yields on threshed fields began to fall, as the harvest moved northward. This indicator normally reaches its peak at the end of July/beginning of August and remains practically unchanged until the end of the harvest.

However, given that most areas sown to grain (excluding corn) have already been harvested (55 percent as of August 5), one can expect average total yields to rise this year by around 30 percent on 1996.
